summary: Two process switches shorten a Delivery's QA gate, both off by default, so every default output and every bound instruction is unchanged. Process switch `own_target_reuse` (`off` | `spot_run`): at `spot_run`, where `pre_handoff_regression` at `touched_suites` gave the freeze an accepted pre-handoff run, QA's final `delivery_verification.py run --kind test --spot-run-file <file>` also takes the Item's own Test Plan targets from that run, under the bindings the earlier stories' targets already need (frozen tree, derived selection and approved command, QA's declared environment, final-evidence age), but for the own targets QA names in the spot-run selection and every own target that is, prefixes or lies under one of them, or under such a target in turn, which the approved test command runs. The runner refuses a spot-run file outside the verification scratch, one that binds another candidate or names a target outside the Item's own Test Plan, and the option with `--fresh`, with any kind but `test` and at `off`; the run's identity records the reused own targets and the spot-run targets under `reused_pre_handoff.own_targets`, evidence approval checks them as recorded, and `approve-item-evidence` adds them to the Item's verification record. Its switch reference asks QA to audit the reused targets with the accepted run's JUnit and output. In one measured project, the story's own cases took 163 of the 227 minutes of QA's final test run, and about 94% of that run repeated tests already run on the identical tree before the handoff. Process switch `qa_gate_order` (`plan_first` | `gate_first`): at `gate_first`, QA starts its first test command of a round in the background, plans, maps and drafts its result while the command works and reads the output only once its plan and coverage matrix are written; in one measured project QA spent 12 to 18 minutes per round writing after a gate of several hours. The `touched_suites` reference now states that the pre-handoff run, like QA's first gate, reports every failing group and counts a group that fails to collect as a failed one.
